4
When One Agent Isn't Enough
ACTIVITY · ROUND 4
Narrow roles are easier to instruct, test and fix
Relay
Router
Fan-out
Manager & team
Maker & checker
Relay
Each agent hands its work to the next
Router
Sends each job to the right specialist
Fan-out
Split decided in advance, done in parallel
Manager & team
A manager decides the split as it goes
Maker & checker
One creates, another reviews
MCP
Model Context Protocol
A2A
Agent2Agent
MCP
Model Context Protocol
Connects an agent to tools and data, such as Google Drive, a CRM or a calendar
A2A
Agent2Agent
Lets one agent work with another, even one built by a different company
5
Diagnose What Went Wrong
ACTIVITY · ROUND 5
Autonomy multiplies mistakes, and every common failure has a design fix
Making things up
Endless loops
Prompt injection
Missing checkpoints
Too much access
Lost instructions
Sprawl
Missing logs
Making things up
FIX
Ground it in trusted sources and ask it to cite them
Endless loops
FIX
Set step limits and clear stop conditions
Prompt injection
FIX
Treat outside content as data, never as instructions
Missing checkpoints
FIX
A person approves anything public, costly or hard to undo
Too much access
FIX
Give only the tools and data the task needs
Lost instructions
FIX
Keep key rules pinned and restate the goal in long tasks
Sprawl
FIX
Keep a register of agents, each with an owner
Missing logs
FIX
Log every action so mistakes can be traced and fixed
6
Make the Design Call
ROUND 6 · DEBRIEF
Give agents specific goals and limits, and keep people in charge
THE DESIGN CALL
Choose the least autonomy that reliably gets the job done
More autonomy costs more, is harder to test and has more ways to fail. Add it only when the task truly needs it.
PUT A PERSON AT ANYTHING
Public
Costly
Hard to undo
